answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks using transitive credit networks where settlement paths ripple through bilateral trust graphs. To harbor counterfeit agents, an attacker incurs the scarce cost of locking liquid capital into verifiable escrow balances for every peer connection. Even when monitoring an agricultural meadow, synthetic nodes cannot transact without authentic credit links. However, this design restricts transaction liquidity and disproportionately empowers well-funded hubs.
